cg-ballast.title: Centre of gravity with the 912 iS
cg-ballast.question: How does the Mod-EZ keep its centre of gravity inside the book envelope now that the 912 iS is lighter than the book engine?

book_choice.text: The book defines the CG envelope as 97.0 to 103.0 inches and prints sample loadings as its own check (the light pilot sample prints 103.96, aft of the 103.0 limit); the sample rows carry no ballast.

options.label: Book engine and loading (baseline)

facts.text: Calculator output on the book's own sample loadings (no private weights); landing is with the 30 minute reserve; coolant and radiator weight are not included and the engine CG arm is assumed equal to the book engine's. Book engine, heavy pilot solo (210 lb): landing CG 100.3 in, forward margin +3.3 in; two adults: +3.7 in

Solo, rear seat empty, mission fuel and baggage, reserve only at landing; solo pilot weight at the 97.0 in forward limit: 292 lb. Landing margin at 120 lb +7.3 in, 160 lb +5.4 in, 200 lb +3.6 in, 220 lb +2.8 in. Public weight range, no owner weights
Book engine, light pilot (135 lb): CG 104.0 in at takeoff, aft of the 103.0 in limit, as in the book's own sample

Loading matrix over the public range (solo 120 to 220 lb, two up, no baggage or a light bag, full, mission and reserve fuel, at takeoff and landing; no owner weights). Forward limit worst: +2.8 in (solo 220 lb, light overnight bag, mission fuel, landing). Aft limit worst: 1.6 in outside (solo 120 lb, no baggage, mission fuel, landing). Gross worst: 173 lb outside (two up 220 lb front, 220 lb rear, light overnight bag, full fuel, takeoff). Solo pilots forward: heavier solo pilots break the limit above 292 lb; aft: lighter solo pilots break the limit below 161 lb; gross: heavier solo pilots break the limit above 267 lb.

options.why: baseline: the envelope and loadings the book itself prints; the 912 iS changes where the empty CG sits

options.label: No change, publish a loading limit

facts.text: Calculator output on the book's own sample loadings (no private weights); landing is with the 30 minute reserve; coolant and radiator weight are not included and the engine CG arm is assumed equal to the book engine's. 912 iS, heavy pilot solo: landing CG 96.8 in, forward margin -0.2 in (forward of the 97.0 in limit); two adults: +0.9 in; light pilot: +3.3 in

Solo, rear seat empty, mission fuel and baggage, reserve only at landing; solo pilot weight at the 97.0 in forward limit: 202 lb. Landing margin at 120 lb +3.9 in, 160 lb +1.9 in, 200 lb +0.1 in, 220 lb -0.7 in. Public weight range, no owner weights

Loading matrix over the public range (solo 120 to 220 lb, two up, no baggage or a light bag, full, mission and reserve fuel, at takeoff and landing; no owner weights). Forward limit worst: 0.7 in outside (solo 220 lb, light overnight bag, mission fuel, landing). Aft limit worst: +0.8 in (two up 120 lb front, 220 lb rear, no baggage, full fuel, takeoff). Gross worst: 96 lb outside (two up 220 lb front, 220 lb rear, light overnight bag, full fuel, takeoff). Solo pilots forward: heavier solo pilots break the limit above 202 lb; aft: lighter solo pilots break the limit below 95 lb; gross: heavier solo pilots break the limit above 344 lb.

options.why: kept: costs no weight, but a heavy pilot flying solo is outside the envelope (see the solo crossing weight), so the airplane would need a maximum-front-seat-weight or minimum-passenger rule; two adults stay inside by only 0.9 in

options.label: Fixed aft ballast

facts.text: Calculator output on the book's own sample loadings (no private weights); landing is with the 30 minute reserve; coolant and radiator weight are not included and the engine CG arm is assumed equal to the book engine's. 14.6 lb at the engine's CG arm (141.05 in) brings the heavy solo case to +0.5 in; two adults already hold that margin. The ballast arm is an assumption
Aft check with the same change, light pilot: highest CG 101.8 in against the 103.0 in aft limit, inside

Solo, rear seat empty, mission fuel and baggage, reserve only at landing; solo pilot weight at the 97.0 in forward limit: 219 lb. Landing margin at 120 lb +4.6 in, 160 lb +2.6 in, 200 lb +0.8 in, 220 lb -0.0 in. Public weight range, no owner weights
With that ballast the heavy solo landing CG is 97.5 in and empty weight rises by the same 14.6 lb, which comes off useful load

Loading matrix over the public range (solo 120 to 220 lb, two up, no baggage or a light bag, full, mission and reserve fuel, at takeoff and landing; no owner weights). Forward limit worst: 0.0 in outside (solo 220 lb, light overnight bag, mission fuel, landing). Aft limit worst: +0.4 in (two up 120 lb front, 220 lb rear, no baggage, full fuel, takeoff). Gross worst: 111 lb outside (two up 220 lb front, 220 lb rear, light overnight bag, full fuel, takeoff). Solo pilots forward: heavier solo pilots break the limit above 219 lb; aft: lighter solo pilots break the limit below 108 lb; gross: heavier solo pilots break the limit above 329 lb.

options.why: kept: simple and testable, at a direct cost in useful load; ballast that is not fixed to the structure is a loading error waiting to happen

options.label: Move the battery aft

facts.text: Calculator output on the book's own sample loadings (no private weights); landing is with the 30 minute reserve; coolant and radiator weight are not included and the engine CG arm is assumed equal to the book engine's. The ledger carries a 19 lb larger battery at fuselage station 11 in the nose (a derived row); moving it to 141.05 in aft changes the heavy solo margin to +2.6 in and two adults to +3.1 in
Aft check with the same change, light pilot: highest CG 103.6 in against the 103.0 in aft limit, OUTSIDE the envelope

Solo, rear seat empty, mission fuel and baggage, reserve only at landing; solo pilot weight at the 97.0 in forward limit: 267 lb. Landing margin at 120 lb +6.9 in, 160 lb +4.8 in, 200 lb +2.9 in, 220 lb +2.0 in. Public weight range, no owner weights
Whether the book airplane carries the larger battery in its 730 lb empty weight (the ledger notes it may carry the small one); if it carries the small one the figures above are an upper bound

Loading matrix over the public range (solo 120 to 220 lb, two up, no baggage or a light bag, full, mission and reserve fuel, at takeoff and landing; no owner weights). Forward limit worst: +2.0 in (solo 220 lb, light overnight bag, mission fuel, landing). Aft limit worst: 1.3 in outside (solo 120 lb, no baggage, full fuel, takeoff). Gross worst: 96 lb outside (two up 220 lb front, 220 lb rear, light overnight bag, full fuel, takeoff). Solo pilots forward: heavier solo pilots break the limit above 267 lb; aft: lighter solo pilots break the limit below 151 lb; gross: heavier solo pilots break the limit above 344 lb.

options.why: kept: ballast that is already carried, but it pushes the light pilot case toward or past the aft limit (see the aft check), needs longer cable runs, and is an upper bound if the book empty weight carries the small battery

options.label: Move the engine installation aft

facts.text: Calculator output on the book's own sample loadings (no private weights); landing is with the 30 minute reserve; coolant and radiator weight are not included and the engine CG arm is assumed equal to the book engine's. Moving the engine's installed CG 3.8 in aft of the book arm brings the heavy solo case to +0.5 in
Aft check with the same change, light pilot: highest CG 101.8 in against the 103.0 in aft limit, inside

Solo, rear seat empty, mission fuel and baggage, reserve only at landing; solo pilot weight at the 97.0 in forward limit: 219 lb. Landing margin at 120 lb +4.6 in, 160 lb +2.6 in, 200 lb +0.8 in, 220 lb -0.0 in. Public weight range, no owner weights
A mount or cowl change forced by an aft engine (the spec requires it to be called out and analysed)

Loading matrix over the public range (solo 120 to 220 lb, two up, no baggage or a light bag, full, mission and reserve fuel, at takeoff and landing; no owner weights). Forward limit worst: 0.0 in outside (solo 220 lb, light overnight bag, mission fuel, landing). Aft limit worst: +0.4 in (two up 120 lb front, 220 lb rear, no baggage, full fuel, takeoff). Gross worst: 96 lb outside (two up 220 lb front, 220 lb rear, light overnight bag, full fuel, takeoff). Solo pilots forward: heavier solo pilots break the limit above 219 lb; aft: lighter solo pilots break the limit below 109 lb; gross: heavier solo pilots break the limit above 344 lb.

options.why: kept: no added weight, but it moves the propeller and cowl and touches the outer shape, which the roadmap keeps out of scope; 3.8 in is the size of the problem, not a design

cooling.title: Engine cooling for the 912 iS
cooling.question: How is the 912 iS cooled in the Mod-EZ, and where do the radiator, oil cooler and coolant go?

book_choice.text: The book airplane's O-235 is air cooled by cowl air (engine type; not checked against the owner's manual here).

options.label: Air-cooled engine (book)

facts.text: The book engine is the air-cooled Lycoming O-235; it has no liquid cooling system
The 912 iS needs about 1.5 l of coolant for its liquid-cooled cylinder heads, so this layout does not apply to it

options.why: baseline: no coolant system to place; the 912 iS does not use it because its cylinder heads are liquid cooled (the maker lists coolant, a radiator and an expansion tank)

options.label: Radiator and oil cooler forward, ducted from the nose

facts.text: The maker lists the coolant radiator at 1.5 kg (3.3 lb), separate from the 63.6 kg base engine (base engine on p96, radiator on p97)
The maker lists the oil radiator at 1.0 kg (2.2 lb).
The maker lists the oil cooler at 0.6 kg (1.32 lb).
The maker gives the total coolant quantity for the engine as approximately 1.5 l (0.4 US gal).
The maker lists a cooling air baffle at 0.36 kg (0.79 lb); the manual does not say whether this is the tractor or the pusher part
The maker lists the overflow bottle at approximately 0.5 l (0.13 US gal).
The maker says an aluminium tube with a 25 mm (1 in) inner diameter can be used instead of longer coolant hoses, and lists inner diameter 25 mm in that tube's specification.
The maker's coolant capacity table lists a 2 m coolant hose with an inner diameter of 18 mm.
SI-912 i-001R7 permits ethylene-glycol coolant with 50 percent water and does not permit waterless propylene-glycol coolant on the 912 i Series.
SI-PAC-014 Revision 1 states a maximum weight of 0.82 kg for the extra-large oil radiator.
Duct size, drag and the real pusher airflow for a nose radiator on this airframe are not sourced

options.why: kept: judgment: a forward radiator has the easiest air supply, but the coolant and oil lines would run the length of the fuselage and its mass sits forward of the engine, which moves the CG forward (geometry, not sourced)

electrical.title: Electrical system for the 912 iS
electrical.question: How is the 912 iS powered and charged, and what in the book panel, wing wiring and battery shelf has to change?

book_choice.text: The book airplane's electrical system is the plans' battery, alternator and panel wiring (steps f22; not checked against the owner's manual here).

options.label: Book single bus, one alternator, one battery

facts.text: The engine-management electrical system is isolated from the rest of the aircraft.
The book wiring does not provide an isolated engine ground, the engine-management supply path or the ammeter the maker requires, so it cannot be kept unchanged

options.why: baseline: judgment: the book wiring was drawn for an engine that needs no electrical supply to run; the 912 iS has its own engine electrics (two lanes, generators, a backup switch) whose ground must be kept separate from the airframe ground

options.label: Isolated engine bus, one aircraft battery with a backup switch

facts.text: The engine-management electrical system is isolated from the rest of the aircraft.
Airframe ground and EMS ground must not be interconnected.
The fuse box has separate plug connections X1 (LANE A) and X2 (LANE B), which ensure power distribution to the EMS.
Generator A (14.2 V/16 A) supplies the EMS after the system check and generator B (14.2 V/30 A) supplies the aircraft instruments and charges the battery.
The aircraft battery must be at least 16 Ah and must hold at least 9 V on the ECU bus during start-up.
The battery technical data require at least 350 A cold-cranking amperes at -18 °C (SAE J537).
If both EMS alternators fail, the 2012 operators manual says to switch on the backup battery switch so the aircraft battery supplies power.
The aircraft manufacturer must provide an ammeter because the EMS does not monitor generator-B charging.
The 2020 installation manual requires a slow-blowing 50 A fuse or circuit breaker for the rectifier regulator.

options.why: kept: one battery to carry, fed through the maker's backup switch when both engine generators fail; the battery must meet the maker's minimum

options.label: Isolated engine bus with its own backup battery

facts.text: The engine-management electrical system is isolated from the rest of the aircraft.
Airframe ground and EMS ground must not be interconnected.
The fuse box has separate plug connections X1 (LANE A) and X2 (LANE B), which ensure power distribution to the EMS.
Generator A (14.2 V/16 A) supplies the EMS after the system check and generator B (14.2 V/30 A) supplies the aircraft instruments and charges the battery.
The aircraft battery must be at least 16 Ah and must hold at least 9 V on the ECU bus during start-up.
The battery technical data require at least 350 A cold-cranking amperes at -18 °C (SAE J537).
If both EMS alternators fail, the 2012 operators manual says to switch on the backup battery switch so the aircraft battery supplies power.
A separate engine backup battery is the builder's option, not something the maker's text requires; its mass, size and position are not sourced

options.why: kept: the engine does not depend on the airframe battery, at the cost of a second battery and its mass and mounting

options.label: Battery of the book airplane

facts.text: Which battery the book empty weight carries (the mass ledger notes it may be the small one) is not sourced

options.why: baseline: the mass the book empty weight may or may not already include; not sourced

options.label: Lithium iron phosphate battery, 15.6 Ah class

facts.text: The EarthX ETX900 product-spec PDF lists weight of 4.9 lb (2.2 kg).
The EarthX ETX900 product-spec PDF lists capacity of 15.6 Ah.
The EarthX ETX900 product-spec PDF lists dimensions 6.5 x 3.1 x 6.6 in (166 x 79 x 168 mm).
15.6 Ah is below the maker's 16 Ah minimum for the aircraft battery; the maker's note leaves a lower-capacity choice to the aircraft manufacturer, so maker agreement is not stated as required
The maker's note says the choice of a lower-capacity battery is up to the aircraft manufacturer, and that extra electrical loads affect battery performance during starting.

The maker says a lithium-ion aircraft battery should only be used with a suitable battery management system, that responsibility then lies with the aircraft manufacturer, and that the aeronautical authority's approval may be necessary.
Its cold-cranking amps and internal resistance against the maker's limits (350 A at -18 C, 10 mohm) are not checked here

options.why: kept: light at 4.9 lb, but its 15.6 Ah is just under the maker's 16 Ah minimum

options.label: Lithium iron phosphate battery, 12.4 Ah class

facts.text: EarthX lists the ETX680C mass as 3.9 lb (1.8 kg) at 13.2 V.
EarthX ETX680C is rated 12.4 Ah at the 1C rate, in a 5.9 x 3.4 x 4.5 in LiFePO4 case.
12.4 Ah is below the maker's 16 Ah minimum for the aircraft battery; the maker's note leaves a lower-capacity choice to the aircraft manufacturer
The maker's note says the choice of a lower-capacity battery is up to the aircraft manufacturer, and that extra electrical loads affect battery performance during starting.

The maker says a lithium-ion aircraft battery should only be used with a suitable battery management system, that responsibility then lies with the aircraft manufacturer, and that the aeronautical authority's approval may be necessary.
Its cold-cranking amps and internal resistance against the maker's limits (350 A at -18 C, 10 mohm) are not checked here

options.why: kept: very light at 3.9 lb, but 12.4 Ah is well below the maker's 16 Ah minimum

options.label: Sealed lead-acid (AGM) battery, 16 Ah class

facts.text: Odyssey lists the PC680 at 16 Ah on both the 20-hour and 10-hour rates.
Odyssey lists the PC680 at 15.4 lb, 7.2 in long, 3 in wide, 6.4 in high including terminals, and 6.6 in container height.
Odyssey lists the ODS-AGM16L (PC680) at 12 V.
The maker limits the aircraft battery's internal resistance to a maximum of 10 mohm at -18 C.
Its cold-cranking amps and internal resistance against the maker's limits are not checked here

options.why: kept: meets the maker's 16 Ah figure, at 15.4 lb the heaviest choice; its cold-cranking and internal resistance are not checked here

fuel-system.title: Fuel system for the 912 iS
fuel-system.question: How is fuel delivered to the 912 iS: pressure, return line, filtering and vapor-lock protection on a pusher?

book_choice.text: The book airplane's engine is carbureted and its fuel plumbing is built under the fuel-system steps (not checked against the owner's manual here).

options.label: Book carburetor feed

facts.text: EASA TCDS E.121 sets the 912 iSc Sport fuel pressure at 2.8 to 3.2 bar (the TCDS covers the iSc Sport series; the iS Sport shares the injection system)
A carburetor gravity or low-pressure feed does not supply 2.8 to 3.2 bar and has no return line, so the book plumbing cannot feed the 912 iS unchanged

options.why: baseline: simple, but built for a carburetor; judgment: it would need a pressurized feed and a return line to suit the injected engine (derived from the maker's pressure figure)

options.label: Pumped feed with a return line to the strake tank

facts.text: EASA TCDS E.121 Issue 17 sets 912 iSc Sport fuel pressure at 2.8 to 3.2 bar.
Two electric fuel pumps are connected in series with bypass valves, and the engine runs on either or both.
The coarse and fine filter mesh sizes (previously recorded as 50 to 67 micron and 8 to 12 micron) were not found on the installation manual pages checked; page unresolved
Fine filter requirement: see the coarse filter entry; page unresolved
The non-drainable low point guidance for feed, return and vent lines was not found on the installation manual pages checked; page unresolved
The maker says fuel lines on the suction side of the fuel pump must be insulated against heat in the engine compartment and routed away from hot engine components, for prevention of vapor locks.
Fuels with more than 10 percent ethanol are not permitted.
The maker's minimum inner diameter for the fuel return line is 7.5 mm (0.3 in).
The maker recommends a restricted bypass line between the pump module outlet and the return line to vent air from the fuel system.
The statement that vapor bubbles in the return line must be vented to atmosphere was not found on the installation manual pages checked; page unresolved
The engine side-view callout naming separate tractor and pusher return connections was not found on the installation manual pages checked; page unresolved
The routing of a return line from the engine to the strake tanks, its length and pressure drop, are not sourced

options.why: kept: the maker's architecture, with two pumps and a return connection; the cost is a return line along the full feed run and a return fitting in the strake tank

options.label: Pumped feed with a small header tank and a return line to it

facts.text: EASA TCDS E.121 Issue 17 sets 912 iSc Sport fuel pressure at 2.8 to 3.2 bar.
Two electric fuel pumps are connected in series with bypass valves, and the engine runs on either or both.

powerplant-fuel-resin.title: Powerplant, fuel and tank resin
powerplant-fuel-resin.question: Which engine, on which fuel, and with which tank resin, for the Mod-EZ?

book_choice.text: the book airplane uses the Lycoming O-235, two wing tanks totalling 52 gal, aviation gasoline, and a maximum true cruise of 161 kt at 75 percent power

options.label: Lycoming O-235

facts.text: 243 lb dry incl. starter and generator
5.8 gal/h at 65 percent, 77 hp
the manual warns that autogas can dissolve the epoxy in the fuel tanks

options.why: baseline, kept so the lineage is complete.

options.label: UL350i

facts.text: 118 hp, ready-to-fly 78.4 kg (173 lb)
mogas minimum 95 RON (91 AKI) below serial 223501, 91 RON (87 AKI) above, 100LL allowed if mogas is unavailable
estimated cruise about 18 L/h
ethanol limit

options.why: kept: about 70 lb lighter installed than the book engine on the maker's ready-to-fly weight, so the tail gets lighter and the empty CG moves forward; runs on mogas; its ethanol limit is the open question. Weight bases differ between candidates (ready-to-fly, operational, a build-up of listed parts), so the weights are not strictly like for like

options.label: UL350iS

facts.text: operational weight 79.5 kg (175 lb) shared with UL350i
power and fuel specifics not verified

options.why: kept: same weight class as the UL350i; its power and fuel numbers have not been verified, so it is scored with unknowns

options.label: Rotax 912iS

facts.text: 63.6 kg with gearbox plus add-ons
16.5 L/h (4.3 gal/h) at 75 percent
more than 10 percent ethanol is not permitted
coolant and radiator weight

options.why: kept: a published fuel flow at 75 percent power (69 hp), close to the mission cruise power; the maker limits ethanol to 10 percent, which ties it to the tank-resin question; coolant and radiator weight are not yet known

options.label: Rotax 915iS

facts.text: The EASA data sheet gives 84,6 kg dry for the 915 iSc2 A, on a larger include list than the maker card
141 hp for 5 min and 82.2 kg with gearbox, turbo, intercooler and exhaust on the maker page
Maker deck row at 5500 rpm: 87,47 kW burns 26,53 kg/h (about 303 g/kWh); the deck prints kg/h only
TBO 1200 h or 15 years, whichever comes first
coolant and radiator weight

options.why: kept, not chosen: about 35 lb heavier installed than the 912 iS on a similar build-up basis and more power than the mission needs; its fuel flow is derived from one maker deck row, so the range figure is rough

options.label: Rotax 916iS

facts.text: The EASA data sheet gives 85.8 kg dry for the 916 iSc2 A
160 hp and 85.8 kg with gearbox, turbo, intercooler and exhaust on the maker page
Maker deck row at 5500 rpm: 89,96 kW burns 22,48027 kg/h (250 g/kWh); the deck prints kg/h only
TBO 2,000 hrs
coolant and radiator weight

options.why: kept, not chosen: about 38 lb heavier installed than the 912 iS on a similar build-up basis and more power than the mission needs; its fuel flow is derived from one maker deck row, so the range figure is rough

options.label: DeltaHawk DHK180

facts.text: 335 lb (151 kg) estimated

options.why: dropped, the wrong direction for this CG; can be reopened.

options.label: Electric

facts.text: a flown electric Long-EZ carried a 525 lb pack, 450 V 80 Ah
The flown pack stored 36 kWh (450 V x 80 Ah = 36,000 Wh) in 525 lb (238 kg): about 151 Wh/kg at pack level
a 500 Wh/kg cell is a company claim, cell level only

Method: shaft power 52 kW at 150 kt (cube-law scaling of the manual's 161 kt at 75 percent of 115 hp) over 0.96 motor efficiency for 2.5 h is about 136 kWh; at 500 Wh/kg that is about 272 kg (600 lb) of cells before pack structure and reserve

options.why: dropped for now: the numbers do not close the 300 nm mission with a pack that has flown (151 Wh/kg) or a claimed cell (500 Wh/kg, cell level); kept so it can be reopened when cells improve

options.label: Hybrid

facts.text: no homebuilder hybrid kit with a published price was found

options.why: none found: no homebuilder hybrid kit with a published price turned up in the sweep (not independently re-checked); kept so it can be reopened

options.label: UL94 Ethanol-Free

facts.text: UL94 is ethanol-free and weighs 5.87 lb/gal

options.why: kept: removes the ethanol question, but no source shows how the book tank resin behaves in UL94, so the resin choice stays open

implies.tank_resin: No source tests UL94 on the book's epoxy tanks, so keeping the conventional tank resin is unconfirmed.

options.label: Mogas E10

facts.text: ethanol can partly dissolve resins in composite tanks

In a builder's 18-month immersion test (54 coupons, two per test) of E-Z Poxy, MGS and Jeffco epoxies in 100LL and 8.4 percent ethanol mogas, none showed visible deterioration; all gained some weight, and post-cure mattered more than brand. Small sample, not a long-term or maker rating

options.why: kept: the common automotive fuel, but ethanol can partly dissolve some composite-tank resins (judgment: the book's tank resin is not shown safe), so this path needs a tank resin that is shown to hold up, with a good post-cure (the rehearsal player carries an open placeholder for it); vapor lock in a hot pusher engine bay is a further judgment-level concern with no source here

implies.tank_resin: Ethanol can partly dissolve some composite-tank resins, so this path needs a tank resin shown to hold up in E10 with a good post-cure; which resin is not yet decided.

positions.reasoning: The Rotax 912iS is the only candidate with a verified cruise fuel flow of 16.5 L/h at 75% power <rotax-912is-om:p1>. The 915iS and 916iS offer more power, but their cruise fuel flows are unknown <rotax-915is-card:p1, rotax-916is-page:p1>, making them speculative 'waste' for this mission. The UL350i is lighter but its fuel specifics are not fully verified <ulpower-ul350i:p1>.

Choosing Mogas E10 introduces a risk where ethanol can dissolve resins in composite tanks <bmaa-sb2695:p1>. While a small-scale test showed some epoxies held up <kitplanes-tank-epoxy-2018:p1>, the compatibility of the specific book tank resin with UL94 is unknown <ul94-ethanol-free:p1>. UL94 is ethanol-free <swift-ul94-faq:p1>, making it the safer structural choice, though the final decision depends on the unconfirmed behavior of the epoxy tanks in UL94.

The Rotax 912iS specifically prohibits more than 10 percent ethanol <rotax-fuel-si:p1>. Using UL94 ethanol-free <swift-ul94-faq:p1> avoids the ethanol-related resin dissolution risks associated with Mogas E10 <bmaa-sb2695:p1>.

No flight test data is available to verify the cruise fuel flows for the higher-power Rotax models (915iS/916iS) or the UL350i average <rotax-915is-card:p1, rotax-916is-page:p1, ulpower-ul350i:p1>. A common-power model for each engine is required to close the paper case. (uncited)
The baseline for the mission is the Lycoming O-235, which uses aviation gasoline and provides a maximum true cruise of 161 kt at 75% power <om-1980:p15>.

propeller.title: Propeller
propeller.question: Which kind of propeller does the Mod-EZ run behind the 912 iS gearbox?

book_choice.text: The book allows only light-weight fixed-pitch solid wood propellers; constant speed, variable pitch and metal propellers are not recommended because a pusher propeller would need extensive development and vibration testing.

options.label: Fixed-pitch solid wood (the book)

facts.text: For the O-235 the owner's manual lists 58 in diameter with 72 in pitch (cruise prop) or 66 in pitch (climb prop)
The designers prefer the climb prop for the best takeoff performance
The airplane's designers later found 62 in diameter by 66 in pitch best for the O-235 on two airplanes with several hundred hours, larger than the plans back page
Static rpm at full throttle must be at least 2450 for normal takeoff performance (an O-235 figure)
Rotation direction of the book propeller
Weight of the book wood propeller

options.why: baseline: the only type the book approves for the pusher; it is matched to a direct-drive engine, not to a geared one

options.label: Fixed-pitch carbon with wood core

facts.text: Catto lists Long EZ propellers with a carbon structure and wood core: two-blade 66 in for 180-200 hp and 64 in for 150-160 hp, three-blade 60 in, and says most canards need a 6 in or 8 in extension
The 912 iS propeller shaft turns counter clockwise looking towards the face of the flange

Inference: if the flange face points aft on a pusher (no reverse-rotation variant fitted), the propeller turns counter clockwise seen from behind, a left-turning pusher propeller; a reseller guide says pushers run a left turning propeller on the Rotax 912 family
Catto statement for the Rotax 912 iS, weight and price

options.why: kept: closest to the book (fixed pitch, wood in the structure), but no source ties it to this engine or to a geared 5800 rpm drive

options.label: Ground-adjustable composite

facts.text: Sensenich 3B0R5 pusher blades (L68C): 68 in maximum and 64 in minimum diameter, 9.0 lb without spacer, approved for Rotax 912, 912S, 912iS and 914 series reduction drives, 5800 rpm engine, 80-115 hp
Sensenich 2A0R5/L69E two-blade pusher: 69 in maximum and 65 in minimum, 10.5 lb, same engine list
The 912 iS gearbox ratio is 2.4286 and the propeller moment of inertia window is 1500 to 6000 kg cm2
The 912 iS propeller shaft turns counter clockwise looking towards the face of the flange

Inference: if the flange face points aft on a pusher (no reverse-rotation variant fitted), the propeller turns counter clockwise seen from behind, a left-turning pusher propeller; a reseller guide says pushers run a left turning propeller on the Rotax 912 family

Maximum takeoff engine speed 5800 rpm over the 2.4286 ratio is about 2388 propeller rpm. That is a ceiling, not a static reading, and the book's 2450 static minimum is a direct-drive O-235 check that does not transfer to a geared engine
Approval of any of these for a Long-EZ airframe, and the pitch to set

options.why: kept: the maker table found that names the 912 iS and has pusher blades; pitch can be set on the ground to fit the geared engine, but the book does not approve non-wood propellers for this airplane

options.label: Constant speed (hydraulic governor)

facts.text: MT-Propeller lists the MTV-34 hydraulic constant-speed propeller for the Rotax 912/914 series and the 915 iS, three-blade 9 kg (19.8 lb) plus a 1 kg governor
On the certified Sport series the iSc3 variant has the hydraulic governor drive (64,4 kg) and the iSc2 has a fixed-propeller flange (63,6 kg)
The book does not recommend constant speed or variable pitch propellers for the pusher, citing aerodynamic-induced vibration and the development testing needed
Pusher approval for the MTV-34 and a Long-EZ installation

options.why: kept: widest operating range, but it needs the governor-drive engine variant and goes against the book's explicit caution, so it needs its own vibration evidence

options.label: Electric constant speed (Airmaster)

facts.text: The listed Airmaster AP332 configuration is a clockwise tractor, 70 in, 25 lbs, for Rotax 912, 912S and 914; no pusher configuration appears on the page
Airmaster pusher configuration for the 912 iS
A 25 lb hub is heavy against the 9 to 10 lb ground-adjustable composites, which would matter for the empty weight and for where the weight sits

options.why: none found: no pusher configuration turned up on the page; kept so it can be reopened

options.label: Metal fixed pitch

facts.text: The book does not recommend metal propellers for the pusher, citing aerodynamic-induced vibration

options.why: dropped on the book's own caution; no other source was found either way
